capability: Prove a bounded minimum-bar plan with explicit between-piece kerf and a search budget.
pain: Greedy allocation can waste a board, while a search cutoff must not be presented as proven optimal.
query: bin packing; cutting stock; official OR-Tools reference follow
contract: Strict JSON stock_length, kerf, pieces. Integer lengths1..1000000, kerf0..1000000;1..24 expanded pieces with unique printable IDs and optional quantity. Unlimited identical stock lengths. Kerf is charged only between adjacent pieces, never at ends. Transform length+kerf into bins of stock+kerf; first-fit decreasing upper bound, valid total-capacity lower bound and exhaustive branch search with equal-free-space symmetry pruning. An optimal claim requires reaching the lower bound or completing search. Oversized pieces return infeasible/exit1; budget exhaustion returns exit2 without a plan or optimality claim.
limits: 64 KiB JSON,250000 search nodes maximum. One stock length, no stock availability/cost objective,2D layouts, end trim, grain, saw sequencing or machine control. The mathematical kerf convention must match the intended planning task; this is not manufacturing certification.
acceptance: Greedy3 versus proven2 counterexample; independent brute-force oracle across small multisets and kerfs; every piece exactly once; conservation, quantities, infeasible inputs and budget refusal.
notes: OR-Tools provides much broader optimization and was found by following its official bin-packing example, not as the top cutting-stock query hit. Opcut is adjacent2D guillotine cutting; csp and stock-cutting are material-planning alternatives. We do not claim faster search, better industrial plans or missing competitor optimality.
overlap: Owned bom-rollup-ledger totals material demand; capacity-cut-report is a network min-cut. Neither solves integer board packing with kerf and an explicit optimality condition.
expected: Exit0: six pieces6,5,3,2,2,2 in stock10 need two bars; the reported first-fit upper bound is three.
